tagline: A chromoprotein-keratin-binding-peptide fusion that colours hair and repairs it in the same step
summary: Baltimore Biocrew, based at the Baltimore Underground Science Space community lab, engineered fusion proteins joining chromoproteins (aeblue, UM) to keratin-binding peptides so that a semi-permanent dye deposits colour while reinforcing the hair shaft. The entrepreneurship work was run through iGEM's Venture Creation Labs curriculum, the same incubator route their 2023 project RhizeUp took, and it produced an OKR table with numeric key results, a scored risk register, a US-specific patent strategy and a competitor map. Market evidence rests on two IRB-approved consumer surveys (56 then 54 responses, translated into Chinese and Filipino) plus named interviews with a cosmetics founder, two L'Oreal North America hair-colour-lab staff, a cosmetology student and the Boeke Lab at NYU Langone. They were nominated for Best Entrepreneurship in the High School section.

dry.frameworks: iGEM Venture Creation Labs curriculum as the scaffold, Golden Circle, Unique Value Proposition, Lean Business Model Canvas, SWOT, a seven-phase Objectives and Key Results table with business-day estimates and fixed-cost lines, a risk register with a published 1-5 impact x 1-5 likelihood scoring rubric and named owners, direct and indirect and future competitor tiers, and the iGEM judging ballot answered question by question.
dry.dataviz: Interactive click-through SWOT, a nine-slide pitch deck embedded as a carousel, a lean canvas, a long-term impact-assessment graphic, a 2027-2029 timeline, and a horizontally scrollable OKR and risk table. Survey results are reported as percentages and cross-tabulated by language group and age.
dry.datascience: Two-round survey analysis with a genuine iteration: a bimodal distribution on grey-coverage priority in Survey 1 (a quarter rating it 1, nearly half rating it 10) was hypothesised to be two age cohorts, and Survey 2 confirmed it by adding age, hair type and prior chemical-treatment questions. Reported figures include 64.3 percent rating less hair damage a 10/10 priority, 89 percent rating it 8 or above, 50 percent using at-home boxed kits and only 25.9 percent relying solely on salons.

good.publicEngagement: Surveys were deliberately multilingual, translated into Chinese and Filipino to reach their own communities, and the results split cleanly by language and age in ways that changed the product thesis: younger English-speaking respondents wanted fashion blues, pinks and purples, which happens to be what their chromoproteins produce, while older Chinese and Filipino respondents wanted grey coverage and natural shades. They also found that the phrase 'genetically engineered' on a label worried more respondents than it attracted, with several linking it to harmful chemicals or illness, and responded by planning a consumer FAQ booklet distributed through partner salons instead of a call centre. They presented at the July 2026 Mid-Atlantic Meetup alongside eight other regional teams.
good.ihp: A Closed-Loop Framework structured each stakeholder conversation into relevance, insight, integration and future question. IRB approval from the BUGSS Board of Directors was obtained before surveying, which is unusual rigour at high-school level. Specific conversations changed specific decisions: Savannah Shumaker (chemist, co-founder and CEO of Eight Count Cosmetics) pushed branding toward audience values and simplified their science communication, and suggested contacting cosmetology schools, which led to Rachel Lu; Lindsay Menzer and Yun Yong Jang (L'Oreal Hair North America, Head of Hair Color Lab) flagged patenting during early testing, which launched the US patent-strategy investigation; the Boeke Lab at NYU Langone recommended storage conditions for chromoproteins, prompting a preservation study; and a question from another team at the Mid-Atlantic Meetup about pH and temperature sensitivity, which they had deprioritised, is what sent them to the Boeke Lab in the first place.
good.realWorld: This is a credible early-stage venture plan with the finance section still hollow. What is genuinely strong is the execution scaffolding. The OKR table is the best artefact: it sets falsifiable targets with costs and durations attached, including catalogue 15 salons statewide, a minimum of 10 qualitative interviews, at least 5 Letters of Intent, 10 investor pitches, 10,000 dollars from stakeholder investment plus research grants, cell viability above 70 percent in cytotoxicity assays, dye longevity of 40 wash cycles, protein stability at 50 degrees C, 1,000 sales per month and two new production labs in other mid-Atlantic states. Named funding targets are real and local (Wexford SciTech Venture Fund, TEDCO grants, Connect Labs at 4MLK as prospective lab space, youth competitions such as Blue Ocean, Paradigm and Slingshot). Crucially, every one of these is still an aspiration: the Letters of Intent are a key result, not a signed document; the grant is applied for, not won; there is no registered entity, though forming an LLC is floated inside the liability risk row. The regulatory path is the most concretely researched part of the whole analysis and is credible: they identify that the FDA Office of Cosmetics and Colors certifies coal-tar and synthetic colour additives but that a chromoprotein appears to fall into neither bucket, name 21 CFR parts 73 and 74 subpart C, name the Color Certifications Inquiry Branch as the body to ask, and note that certified and uncertified colours carry legally distinct names. The IP strategy is equally specific and actually actionable: a provisional patent on the aeblue-keratin fusion first, converted to a non-provisional within twelve months, with USPTO micro-entity status claimed for an 80 percent fee reduction, and they check their own eligibility against the 262,380 dollar gross-income threshold. Market sizing, by contrast, is the weakest link, resting on Grand View Research hair-colour market reports rather than any bottom-up estimate, with no price point, no cost of goods and no unit economics anywhere. Continuation is plausible rather than secured: they state plainly that as a high-school iGEM team they can never test on human hair, so KeraTINT must pursue third-party testing or operate independently of iGEM after the competition, and they sequence cytotoxicity, pH and thermal assays as the first post-Jamboree work. The precedent helps their case, since the same team's 2023 RhizeUp project went through the same incubator.

gemsTakeaway: Steal the OKR table: every commercialisation objective gets a numeric key result, a business-day estimate and a fixed-cost line, including scientific gates such as cell viability above 70 percent and dye longevity of 40 wash cycles, so a business plan becomes a checklist a successor team can inherit. Also copy getting institutional IRB approval before running consumer surveys, which both protects participants and makes the resulting data citable.
